learning_outcomes.text: Describe the main phases of the casting, welding and adhesive bonding processes.
Identify the critical phases of these processes.
Explain the relationships between structure and defects and operating conditions in the different phases of the processes.
Identify the main conditions and parameters that must be controlled in order to reduce or avoid defects and promote the desired metallurgical structure and mechanical properties.
Apply this knowledge to produce sketches and critique the design of parts to be obtained by these technologies.
Analyze and criticize given manufacturing processes, in the areas of casting, welding and adhesion.
Learn more on your own and develop your scientific and technical skills in these areas.
Knowledge of the main welding and brazing bonding techniques used in the manufacture of carbon steel and carbon/manganese steel structures.
Knowledge of: Main welding technologies used in the national industry and the most significant parameters that control them.
Knowledge of: Technology-specific limitations in relation to other alternative methods.
Knowledge of: Concept of weldability of a material and the main connection difficulties.
Knowledge of: Need to design a part bearing in mind that it will be welded.
Have a general knowledge of the techniques of bonding materials with structural adhesives.
Working in groups and acquiring greater competence in communication strategies (written and oral) and motivation.

syllabus_topics: Main casting alloys and their technological characteristics.
Interfaces.
Germination and growth of new phases and crystals. Casting of cast iron.
Melting and reactions between the liquid refractory metals and the atmosphere.
Solidification, solidification mechanisms and resulting structures in different alloys.
Fast fusion and solidification in welding.
Classes of additive manufacturing processes and main processes used industrially.
Drawing rules and their relationship to defects in castings.
Conventional casting processes.
Design for obtaining castings.
Laboratory wax casting and additive manufacturing.
Additive manufacturing processes, advantages and limitations of these processes.
Properties and classifications of connection processes.
Manual welding with coated electrodes.
Submerged arc welding.
TIG Welding.
MIG / MAG Welding.
Resistance welding.
Brazing.
Weldability of carbon steels and C/Mn steels.
Heat treatments.
Deformations in welding.
Weld costing.
Quality control.
Introduction to adhesive bonding (theory of adhesion, surface preparation, families of adhesives and selection).
Introduction to adhesive bonding (fabrication, control, safety, design and durability).

assessment_methods.method: Group work (report + presentation) of foundry and additive manufacturing
Group work (report + presentation) of welding and adhesive joints

assessment_rules: The final grade (CF) is calculated as: 0.3 * Casting Test + 0.4 * Binding Process Test + 0.2 * Foundry and Additive Manufacturing Group Work + 0.1 * Welding and Adhesive Joints Group Work. The average of the assessment components for Foundry and Additive Manufacturing (Casting test + Foundry group work) as well as for Welding and Adhesive Processes (Binding process test + Welding group work) must have a minimum rating of 7. To obtain attendance, students must attend at least 75% of the practical laboratory (PL) classes. Classification improvement is possible through a final recourse exam for one or both blocks, with the original weights applied.
